content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding connecting an [product_name] to an [product_name] HMI, but couldn't find a clear answer. Here’s my setup: [article_no] – [product_name] software [version_no]; [article_no] – [product_name] software [version_no]; [article_no] – [product_name]; [article_no] – HMI panel. I would like to link these devices directly without an Ethernet switch, due to limited space in my electrical panel. Is there a way to program both the PLC and HMI via direct PC connection, then connect them together without the PC being involved?
Yes, it's possible to make a direct connection.
I've attached a simple example for your reference.

Hi again [user_name], sorry if this is a basic question. I’m trying to connect the HMI to an [product_name] PLC. I tried compressing the files as you did, but my archive is still 3.87 MB. I could only send the ladder diagram. I successfully uploaded ladder logic to the PLC and the HMI code to the HMI, then connected both directly, but communication still isn’t working. Could you supply a complete step-by-step guide?
You can archive your engineering project directly in the software by selecting Project > Archive. This creates a file with a ".zap20" extension, which you can upload for sharing.
The program you uploaded for the [product_name] is just an empty network project.
Found and attached the correct file. Apologies for the earlier mistake.

Be sure to enable S7 access in your configuration file (LSC file). Also, you're assigning memory twice: you use VW0 and also reference bits within VW0 simultaneously. VW0 includes V-bits V0.0 through V1.7.

Hi [user_name], sorry for the late reply. I applied all your suggested changes, but it's still not working. To test, I created a basic setup (image below), but the relay on the [product_name] still won't activate. I also tried steps 7 through 12 from a linked resource, but nothing improved. Thanks for your patience. EDIT: I noticed the LAN LEDs blink green/yellow on both the [product_name] PLC and HMI.

You don't need additional hardware. I downloaded your project and configuration file, updated IP addresses, created a new screen in the HMI project, and changed runtime settings to start with the new screen. You can view the results in the attachment.
Alright, I'll review it. Thanks so much!

There’s finally some progress! Not sure why, but your project files are giving different results. However, when I swap out the inputs for mine, only V1.0 and V1.1 respond. No integer values are being transferred. Attached is my updated version with your modifications. Thanks a lot for your help!
I’m unsure what's wrong with your project or configuration file. Using new screens and variables works well for me.
After another test, I found the issue: delete the recipe and it functions correctly.
Thanks very much for your assistance. That was a strange bug. Now I can finally complete the project!
The key outcome is that everything works now.
Hello again. I attempted to send an emergency signal to the HMI in this project update, but it wasn't received. What steps do I need to take so the HMI will receive the signal?
In your diagram, you send the emergency signal using the network output at address V1.2. In your HMI tag list, the signal is set to I1.2. Do you see where the mismatch is?
Ah, so the V address isn’t tied to either an input or output specifically? Thanks, and sorry for the basic question.
You assigned a digital network output to memory location V1.2. You need to use the same address in the HMI for correct operation.

Initial configuration seemed possible, but ongoing communication failures occurred, despite multiple software tweaks, addressing changes, and troubleshooting steps. Confusion centered around engineering project archives, memory assignments, access permissions, and file handling, complicating the integration process.

There’s a preference for clear step-by-step instructions and reliable operation in this simple setup.
